html:
A battle fought on 28 July 1402 on the Çubuk plain near Ankara, in which Timur crushed the army of the Ottoman sultan Bayezid I and took him prisoner. Bayezid died in captivity the next year.

Bayezid, called the Thunderbolt, had built up Ottoman power fast in the Balkans and Anatolia, and his troops were blockading Constantinople, the capital of the Byzantine Empire (see Bayezid's blockade). Both rulers claimed lordship over the small Turkish states of Anatolia, the beyliks, and they traded insulting letters. At Ankara the Tatars and many Anatolian troops in Bayezid's army went over to Timur, while his Serbian allies and Janissaries fought on.

The defeat almost destroyed the Ottoman Empire. Bayezid's sons fought each other for over a decade, the Ottoman Interregnum, until Mehmed I reunited the state in 1413. Constantinople gained another half century before it fell in 1453. Timur, who did not want to hold Anatolia, gave the beyliks back their lands and turned east to plan an invasion of China, but died in 1405.
